messages:
raj: Heads-up — about to apply a TF change that moves runtime knobs out of the shared ConfigMap into per-model ConfigMaps and wires a KMS-backed secret for feature flags. Running a plan now, can folks eyeball for rollout/downtime risk?

raj: plan excerpt:
```
  # kubernetes_config_map.shared will be replaced
  - resource "kubernetes_config_map" "shared" {
      - data = { ... } -> null
    }

  # kubernetes_config_map.per_model["gpt-medium"] will be created
  + resource "kubernetes_config_map" "per_model" {
      + data = { "runtime_knobs": "..." }
    }

  # kubernetes_secret.feature_flags (managed) will be created
  + resource "kubernetes_secret" "feature_flags" { ... }
```

infra-bot: terraform plan shows: 1 to add, 1 to replace, 0 to destroy. Also note state will record both configmaps.

miriam: quick q — are we changing mount paths? pods expect /etc/config/shared-config currently, will that name disappear?

raj: Not changing mount paths in the first apply. New per-model CMs get created but deployments won't switch names until step 2. Goal: create + secret, then patch deployments to reference new CM names.

dave: If the shared CM is replaced (k8s resource version change) mounts will update in-place but kubelet may reload files without restart. Risk is if keys change name. If keys stay same, zero-downtime likely. Safer: two-step rollout — create new CM, update deployments to mount new CM (canary subset), then delete old.

sophie: +1 to two applies. Also, if we can land the secret creation first, then update a single canary deployment to validate flag lookup against KMS before mass rollout.

raj: Plan to split: (1) apply that creates per-model CMs + secret (no deployment edits), (2) patch canary deployment to new CM name and validate, (3) roll the rest, (4) remove shared CM. Sound ok? :thumbsup:

miriam: LGTM. Add an annotation like `config.redwood/previous-cm: shared-config` on the deployment during canary so rollback is explicit. Also add a short runbook step to rebind the old CM if we need to revert.

infra-bot: FYI — terraform state rename semantics: if resource addresses change, consider `terraform state mv` or ensure new resource has distinct name so we don't accidentally orphan. Also consider `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` on critical configs during the migration window.

raj: Good call. I'll keep `prevent_destroy` while we migrate and then remove it in the final cleanup step. I'll open a PR with the plan output + ordered apply steps and tag owners (miriam, dave, sophie). Scheduling a 10-min rollout window at 03:00 UTC to minimize user traffic. I'll post the PR link here once done.

dave: fine by me. ping me on the PR if you want me to run the canary rollout.

raj: thanks all — will follow up with PR and timeline.

infra-bot: Reminder: if you create `kubernetes_secret` with sensitive data, verify `sensitive = true` in TF and do not print secret data in PR.
